title: Determining Whether a Period is Representative
raw_text:
9/29/26, 9:42 AM
You can only extrapolate from a previous period, if it is representative. Whether a period is representative or not is a result of the
original weighting procedure.

Determining Whether a Period is Representative
Whether a base period is representative or not is determined as follows:
Weighting portion of period = Minimum portion
or
Minimum portion in percent * Length of meter reading period
= Minimum length of base period

«Se Example

e The following meter reading reasons exist:

e O1 Periodic meter reading

e 03 Final meter reading

e O6 Meter reading at move-in (M)

e O8 Meter reading at installation (I)

e 09 Interim meter reading without billing (Y)
e O2 Interim meter reading with billing (Z)

e 10 Control meter reading
e The period length of the portion is 1 year (365 days)
e The minimum portion defined in the rate is 50%

e The minimum requirements to determine whether the base period is representative are determined in the following
way:

Weighting portion of period = Minimum portion

or

Minimum portion in percent (50%) * Length of meter reading period (365 days)
= Minimum length of base period (182.5 days)

In the example, the base period must have a minimum weighting portion of 50% or be at least 182.5 days long in order to be

representative.
